title: Pilot cohort watchpoints and safety contracts (sketch, WIP)
summary: Working sketch: standardize the guardrails, pulse checks and human escalation rituals for small-scale pilot releases (aka pilot cohorts). Focus is on reliability, cost-latency tradeoffs, and clear abort/rollback calculus so product + infra + SRE can run pilots safely with minimal friction.
body:
Purpose:
- Provide a compact operational checklist for ’pilot cohorts’ (10–1,000 users) that teams can reuse for early feature exposure and A/B ballots where latency/cost are sensitive.
- Align cross-functional expectations: who watches what, when to cut traffic, and how to communicate.

Principles (why this is different):
- Small first, instrumented always: pilots should bias toward observability over scale.
- Minimal human overhead: standardized rituals and templates so PM/Eng/Infra don’t reinvent triage.
- Cost-aware gating: avoid surprise token spend by bounding pilot budgets and toggling quantization/packing knobs.

Pilot cohort definitions (examples):
- Micro: 10–100 users or 0.01% global traffic. Use for early UX feedback. Short lived (hours–days).
- Early: 100–1,000 users or 0.1%–1% traffic. Use for interoperability & safety signals. Duration 1–2 weeks typical.
- Holdout: matched control cohort for A/B analysis; size depends on metric sensitivity (see sample-size guidance).

Watchpoints (primary signals to monitor):
- Safety/behavioral: crash/error rate (5xx), hallucination/failure heuristics (language-specific regression triggers), human flags. Threshold: immediate alert if 5xx increases > 2x baseline or absolute > 0.5%.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for in-path model and routing layers. Gate: if p95 increases > 50% of baseline for > 5m, escalate.
- Cost tokens: per-request token distribution and cumulative spend vs pilot budget. Gate: projected spend > budget * 1.1 -> notify.
- Quality metrics: synthetic prompt set (smoke prompts) pass rate. Gate: drop below agreed pass rate (default 90%) -> hold traffic.
- Traffic health: request success ratio, streaming failures, partial payloads.

Pulse schedule (who looks and when):
- T+0 (activation minute 0): shift lead (engineer) confirms routing, smoke prompts green, budget flag set.
- T+5, T+15, T+60: automated dashboard snapshots posted to rollout channel + summary message.
- Days 1–3: twice daily steward check-ins; Days 4–14: daily.
- Always: oncall paging rules active (SRE paged for infra degradation).

Escalation ritual (stepwise):
1) Detection: alert triggers or steward sees anomaly in dashboard.
2) Triage (5–15 min): steward runs check-script (see linked artifacts) to classify issue: infra vs model vs data.
3) Mitigation (15–60 min): apply runway-level mitigation: reduce cohort traffic to 10%, switch to cached variant, or fall back to simpler model.
4) Decision (60–180 min): product + engineering + SRE call to either: continue on reduced exposure, abort and roll back, or expand. Decision documented in ticket.
5) Postmortem: if abort or major incident, write a one-pager within 72h.

Abort calculus (simple rules):
- Abort immediately if any of: data leak detection, PII exfiltration risk, safety classifier breach for > 10 unique users, or regulatory violation.
- Abort if two or more primary watchpoints exceed their thresholds for > 30 minutes despite mitigation.
- Soft hold (reduce to 10%) if single watchpoint spike that is transient or tied to a known deployment artifact.

Traffic shaping knobs (operational controls):
- Exposure percentage: 100% -> 50% -> 25% -> 10%.
- Model variant selection: primary, quantized fallback, cached-prefix variant.
- Token budget cap per-cohort with hard kill at budget exceed.
- Request sampling: enable more verbose telemetry for 1% of requests (trace-level) during pilot.

Telemetry & dashboards (minimum instrument set):
- Per-cohort metrics: requests, unique users, errors, p50/p95/p99 latency, token_count, cost_estimate, synthetic-prompt pass rate.
- Trace links in alert payloads and a prebuilt dashboard template (see linked artifacts).
- Human flags: a simple /rollout-flag command that tags a request id for rapid playback.

Sample size guidance (back-of-envelope):
- For click/accept rate changes ~5 percentage points, cohort sizes of ~2–5k users give detectable signals at 80% power depending on baseline.
- For latency-sensitive gates, rely on p95 shifts; small cohorts can show noise—prefer aggregation windows of 15m for stability.

Experiment analysis plan (fast check list):
- Pre-commit: define primary metric + risk budget (acceptable negative delta).
- Tag traffic and persist cohort ids for analysis.
- Run both quick sanity checks (1–2 days) and final analysis after full pre-specified exposure window.

Communications templates (short):
- Activation message: "Pilot X -> cohort Y enabled at T. Watchpoints: latency, safety, cost. Steward: LEAH. SRE oncall: TEAM-A."
- Abort message: concise cause, immediate action taken, expected follow ups.

Next steps (practical):
- Bake this sketch into a short checklist template and a dashboard template (owner: Marcus).
- Add /rollout-flag hook in traffic-router (owner: Diego).
- Pilot this playbook on an internal feature pilot (target: Mar sprint).

Open questions (for working sessions):
- Default budget vs team budgets: should teams set explicit token budgets per feature or inherit org defaults?
- How aggressive should automatic fallback be before human approval?
- Should we enforce a mandatory canary-only mode for model-architecture changes?

Owner & oncall:
- Playbook owner: Leah Nguyen (product); escalation steward: assigned engineer from owning team; SRE oncall as per page rota.

Notes to self:
- Keep this intentionally lightweight. The goal is repeatability across many small pilots without heavy ceremony.
- Will iterate after 2 real pilots and 1 postmortem.
next_steps: - Convert to a one-page checklist and add to rollout template library.\n- Create dashboard clone and document in Ops wiki.\n- Schedule 30m sync with engineering leads to align default thresholds.
risks: - False positives from noisy telemetry leading to premature aborts.\n- Teams bypassing the checklist for speed.\n- Budget misconfiguration causing unexpected spend.
